dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi! I'm looking for a romance book in the $15 to $30 range. The most important thing for me is that it has an average customer rating of at least 4 out of 5. Can you recommend anything that fits?
dialogue.agent:
Here are three romance books in your $15–$30 range, each with strong customer ratings:

- "The Peacekeeper (Britannia Romanus)" — $19.95, average rating 5.0 (1 review). A historical romance/mystery set in Roman Britain.
- "Transcending Fire" — $23.95, average rating 5.0 (1 review). Features romance, steamy scenes, and undead pirates with lots of plot twists.
- "Keeping Faith" — $17.99, average rating 4.7 (11 reviews). Contemporary romance with the highest number of reviews among these choices.

Would you like more details about any of these books?

products.title: The Peacekeeper (Britannia Romanus)
products.description: Review I have loved every book written by Jess Steven Hughes, historical novels and set in Roman Britain. Where, you say? Read the First four Hughes books, once referred to as the "Sign of the Eagle" series, and find out. Now Hughes has given us a new book, the Peacekeeper. And with it, new branding for his historical adventure series begins in earnest: Henceforth called the "Britannia Romanus" series, the triumph of these earlier volumes is about to be eclipsed with the publication of the Peacekeeper, #5 in this story but a magnificent stand-alone read as well. Why do I recommend the Britannia Romanus series? Because it's that good, good enough to recommend without reservation. Few can do what Hughes does, mixing genres to bring us books that open doors into worlds previously unknown, time after time. Hughes writes a combination of mystery, adventure, suspense and romance seldom equaled. A former Marine and police detective, real-life experience informs every sentence, every page. Those characters breathe and suffer and scheme and love and hate as if they were ripped from history whole cloth. The Peacekeeper is suitable for young and old. At times, Hughes' writing reminds me of Umberto Ecco, at other times, Wallace Breen. With the Peacekeeper, Hughes delivers on the promise of earlier volumes, delivering a deeply-researched historical novel filled with mystery, adventure, romance, and command of his period so strong and effortless, so real, you'll think you've been to Roman Britain yourself! Few can equal Jess Steven Hughes. So come spend some time in Roman Britain with a gifted author whose skill is never obtrusive and whose characters you'll never forget. -- Janet Morris About the Author Jess Steven Hughes brought his lifetime's fascination with ancient Roman history into his debut novel, The Sign of the Eagle. The fascination continues as this has become part of a chain of books called the Britannia Romanus series. This includes The Wolf of Britannia, Part I and Part II. Another historical novel, The Broken Lance, set in Roman Britain and Imperial Rome is the first book of a duo-logy that includes The Peace Keeper. Jess is a retired a police detective sergeant, Long Beach Police Dept, Long Beach, CA. He holds a Masters Degree from the University of Southern California in Public Administration with a minor (my first academic love) in Ancient Mediterranean Civilizations. He also served four years United States Marine Corps (1962/66). As a retired person, Jess believes in keeping very busy. You must stay active mentally, physically and socially. These are a few of the keys to a long and healthy retirement. Writing novels has contributed greatly to my quality of life. He lives with his wife, Liz, on a four-acre mini-farm in Eastern Washington. His hobby is outdoor model railroading. He has an outdoor model railroad that was featured in the June/July 2010 issue of the regional magazine PRIME NORTHWEST (www.primenw.com). Check their website for the article. He was also featured in the Today segment of the Spokane Spokesman-Review, August 18, 2012, ﻿The Longest Chapter﻿, in which he discussed his quest to become a published author. Check the following link for the article. http: //www.spokesman.com/stories/2012/aug/18/the-longest-chapter/ Jess is a member of the Pacific Northwest Writers Association (PNWA) and is active in the Red Ink Fictioneers writers support group in the Spokane, WA area.

products.title: Transcending Fire
products.description: Review "I love the story, and characters. The romance and the sex are perfect and steamy... plot is solid, and I enjoy the undead pirates- they were a nice touch... lots of great twists that keep things interesting." -Dana Hammer, author of The Cannibal's Guide to Fasting About the Author When E. K. is not obsessing over the Transcending Fire universe, she's likely playing with her baby, replicating the latest cooking craze she saw on YouTube, reading the latest Kindle releases, or planting more tropical plants in her garden somewhere in Northeast Florida. She dreams of traveling the world with her husband and son, and maybe, if she's lucky, she'll finally get to build a snowman.

products.title: Keeping Faith
products.description: About the Author Cindy Bradford lives at South Padre Island, Texas on the Laguna Madre, where she enjoys the peacefulness of the Gulf of Mexico. She also spends extended time in her condo in Ruidoso, New Mexico, where she has a view of the mountains and the best of both worlds--a welcomed respite after more than thirty years as a public school educator. Her passions include traveling, gardening, cooking and drinking wine. To learn more and read her blog go to www.DocCBradford.com.

dialogue.user: I'm interested in both "Keeping Faith" and "Transcending Fire." Can you tell me a little more about the storylines of these two, and if there are any particular aspects that make their romance stand out?
dialogue.agent:
Here’s more detail about each book:

- "Keeping Faith": This story centers around Patrick O'Brien, who suffered childhood trauma and struggles with its impact on his relationships. The romance is marked by themes of forgiveness, redemption, and healing, as the main character is finally confronted by a woman determined to uncover the truth and mend their lost love. Their journey is about overcoming betrayal and learning to love again despite a painful past.

- "Transcending Fire": The story follows Alexandra, a warrior princess betrayed by her own commanders. Set in a fantasy world at war, she faces numerous challenges, from enemy capture to forbidden magic, and even undead pirates. The romance stands out for its steamy, passionate elements set amidst action and adventure, featuring a militant prince and high-stakes attraction within a plot of twists and resilience.

Would you like customer reviews or more information on either book?

result.title: Keeping Faith
result.features: Keeping Faith is a story of love found, lost, and found again, of betrayal, forgiveness, redemption and healing. Most of all it holds the bitter truth of how the selfish actions of individuals far transcend the moment. As a ten year old, Patrick O'Brien is abused by his priest. Ashamed and afraid no one will believe him, for years he carries the unspeakable act alone, allowing it to eat at the recesses of his heart, destroying relationships one by one. Finally he is confronted by the one person who is determined to get to the truth no matter what the cost. She has waited almost two decades to unravel his lies, to break down his barriers, and to find out why he was more interested in saving souls than claiming her. When she appears at his door he can no longer run; there's no escaping the past, even if it destroys him.
result.description: About the Author Cindy Bradford lives at South Padre Island, Texas on the Laguna Madre, where she enjoys the peacefulness of the Gulf of Mexico. She also spends extended time in her condo in Ruidoso, New Mexico, where she has a view of the mountains and the best of both worlds--a welcomed respite after more than thirty years as a public school educator. Her passions include traveling, gardening, cooking and drinking wine. To learn more and read her blog go to www.DocCBradford.com.

result.title: Transcending Fire
result.features: Misfortune plagues a warrior princess who goes by the name Alexandra. She spent her youth commanding armies until the cruelest among her commanders turned on her in favor of an usurper masquerading as her cousin. Now, she is faced with a series of life-threatening challenges and one false step could mean the end of a reality that has run out of time. Transcending Fire is the first book in a series that is set in a fractured world that has been torn apart by a hundred year war. On her journey from the battlefield where she is captured and into the heart of an enemy empire she will beguile a militant prince, outwit a band of pirates, employ the use of forbidden necromancy magic and, with the help of a swamp witch, unlock a long forgotten power that was her birthright a hundred years ago.The message of this first book is to rise above insurmountable odds, even when your path is engulfed in flames. She was there the day the war began and ultimately she will bring an end to it.

dialogue.user: Thanks for those summaries! I think I’m leaning a bit towards a more contemporary setting, so "Keeping Faith" sounds appealing. One thing I want to check—since romance and character connection are most important to me, does "Keeping Faith" provide a strong, emotional romance focus, or is it more about overcoming the past and less about the actual relationship?
dialogue.agent:
Customer reviews for "Keeping Faith" highlight that the romance is a central theme and that the emotional connection between the characters is strong and deeply developed. Readers mention being touched emotionally, loving the mix of romance, travel, and character complexity, and eagerly awaiting further development between Faith and Patrick. The romance story is described as compelling, well-written, and woven throughout the book, not overshadowed by the themes of overcoming the past.

Would you like to go ahead with this choice, or do you want to explore further?

top_reviews.title: Compelling and Intriguing!!
top_reviews.text: This book touched on all of my emotions. It gave me a warm fuzzy feeling...sorrow & compassion...laughter...crying...& shock. It grasped my attention on the first page and never let me go. There were so many interesting turns in this book that not only kept me from putting it down but made me long for the sequel. And, the places that Patrick traveled were so interesting. Hurry, Cindy Bradford, we need to see what happens with Faith and Patrick at long last. I am just amazed that this is only your first book to publish. This was well written.

top_reviews.title: Keeping Faith
top_reviews.text: Having known this author for over 30 years, I anxiously awaited her first novel. I was not disappointed.  Now, I await the sequel with the same anxiety.  Cindy captured my attention from the beginning and held it throughout the book.  My normal genre is romance (which was the theme woven throughout the book), but her inclusion of the many sights and places I'll never get to see brought those places vividly to me through her captivating descriptions.  I will definitely be reading the sequel.

top_reviews.title: It just grabbed me.
top_reviews.text: This book was one that I couldn't put down.  I loved the mix of travel, religion, love and fate.  My interest in a book is centered around the complexity of characters and the main characters of this book certainly fulfilled that interest.  I'm waiting for the next one..

dialogue.user: That sounds like exactly what I’m looking for since I really want a romance-driven story. The price and rating both fit my criteria, and it sounds like it delivers on the emotional side too. Based on everything you’ve told me, I feel confident that "Keeping Faith" matches my preferences. <YES>
